audit.why: Poppy 56.51% over 545 games — a clearly winning lane. TRICKY 7.5/10 with an 8.5 carry threat is fair given how little the early lead means once he hits crit items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows gave Tryndamere or Skill the stage against their own text: whys[1] and whys[2] describe Poppy's unconditional wall stun before crit exists, whys[4] says 'even Undying Rage can't beat displacement', whys[5] says your components out-trade him — yet the chart said Tryndamere/Tryndamere/Skill/Tryndamere.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Poppy/Poppy/Skill/Poppy/Poppy/Tryndamere, matching a 56.51% win rate: Poppy owns everything until his crit items.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 to Poppy in both layers as one group, with ratings raised. Row 6 stays Tryndamere.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page twice calls Tryndamere a 'sustain-less kit'. Bloodlust (Q) consumes his Fury to heal him, on a flat 12s — he is one of the most sustain-heavy champions in the lane. Mocking Shout was also described as a plain slow; it only slows enemies whose backs are turned to him.
audit.why: Calling him sustain-less contradicts the page's own anti-heal advice and tells the user their chip is banked when it is not. The Mocking Shout condition changes how you disengage: walking away is what triggers the slow.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust named as the heal with its 12s cooldown and Grievous Wounds tied to it; Mocking Shout's back-turned condition stated; Spinning Slash named as the dash W stops (that interaction was right, just unnamed).

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage was tracked with a duration but no cooldown, and Spinning Slash had no number.
audit.why: 120/100/80s on the R and 12/11/10/9/8s on the dash are what let you time an all-in.
audit.corrected: Both written into dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.why: Packet flagged 'Undying Rage's' in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong name. It is the correct ability name — a false positive, checked against the kit file.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are roughly even as his crit chance and spin damage start ramping while your flat damage stays put, so trade in short bursts and reset rather than extended duels. At 6 your R is the answer to his whole pattern — Keeper's Verdict launches him out of his own all-in or back under your tower, and even his Undying Rage immortality can't save him if he's displaced away from the fight. Save W to ground his E when he dives, and don't waste R on a tap when the full launch undoes his engage entirely.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are roughly even as his crit ramps while your flat damage stays put, so trade in short bursts and reset rather than dueling. Have Grievous Wounds up first: Bloodlust turns his Fury straight into health on a flat 12s and undoes the chip you win. At 6 your R answers his whole pattern — Keeper's Verdict launches him out of his own all-in or back under your tower, and Undying Rage can't save him if he is displaced out of the fight. Save W for his Spinning Slash and don't spend R on a tap.

edits.before: This is where he reclaims the lane. Full-crit Tryndamere spin-kites with W-slow, and his flat-damage shutdown means nothing once your kit value flattens out — your percent-HP Q and CC stay relevant but you can't out-DPS or out-scale him 1v1. Undying Rage makes him nearly impossible to actually kill in a side lane. Group, use your W dash-deny and E-into-wall as team utility, and let your carries finish him rather than dueling him alone.
edits.after: This is where he reclaims the lane. Full-crit Tryndamere kites you with Mocking Shout — which only slows you once your back is turned — and Bloodlust heals off the chip you land, so your percent-HP Q and CC stay relevant but you cannot out-DPS or out-scale him 1v1. Undying Rage makes him nearly impossible to kill in a side lane. Group, use W on his Spinning Slash and E-into-wall as team utility, and let your carries finish him rather than dueling him alone.

notes: The page described Tryndamere as having a 'sustain-less kit' in two places while simultaneously telling the user to build anti-heal. Bloodlust is a flat 12s self-heal off Fury — corrected, with the Grievous Wounds timing attached per the missing-interaction flag. Mocking Shout's slow only applies to enemies with their backs turned, which was never stated. Packet suspectName 'Undying Rage's' is a false positive — the name is correct. Level chart rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 flipped in matched pairs to match both the packet and their own whys.
